newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases as means shored up for T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases as means shored up for T-bills.

text.p: The rouble eased on Wednesday after banks set aside funds for today's government securities sales and dealers said rouble supply remained plentiful despite high turnover on the Treasury bill market.
Today the central bank is auctioning 7.50 trillion roubles of 266-day GKO T-bills and a new three trillion roubles tranche of OFZ bonds.
roubles/dollar Jan 15 midday Jan 15 early Jan 14 close
"There were some signs of rouble shortage beginning yesterday (when funds were set aside for the auctions) but it did not continue today," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Nikolai Zolotaryov said.
Some dealers said the large supply of roubles on the market could be due to an increased but undisclosed issue of money by the central bank.

"Lots of roubles are in the T-bill trading system but the rouble is cheap on the interbank market. This could be a sign of hidden money issue," said United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov.
"But the central bank is sticking to its policy of a slow rouble decline anyway," he said.

The rouble, strictly controlled by the central bank, was not affected by a warning from President Boris Yeltsin's chief doctor Sergei Mironov that his pneumonia was a serious illness which could lead to complications.
Mironov added Yeltsin;s condition has stabilised in the last three days, but he would have to remain in hospital until the end of this week.
